headline: High-risk filesystem and git overlap: Claude Code can write the shared workspace while RisingWave is a mutable data system, creating default-path conflict and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code reads and writes repo files and user-provided directories, and its shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. RisingWave is a data-engineering system with no documented isolation or provenance bridge, so if its outputs are placed in the shared workspace, Claude Code may treat file content as trusted instructions. The pathway is plausible but not directly documented for this pair.
conditions: IF RisingWave outputs are written into the same workspace Claude Code reads
IF Claude Code parses those files as instructions or task context
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Require a human review step before Claude Code consumes RisingWave-generated files
Prefix machine-generated files with a non-executable marker convention
Disable automatic ingestion of workspace files where possible
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between producer and consumer

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, while RisingWave is a data-engineering system that may process sensitive datasets. Because Claude Code shares state via filesystem and git only, any shared workspace can expose data from RisingWave to Claude Code outputs. RisingWave has no documented local-only boundary here, so the pair creates a realistic workspace leakage path.
conditions: IF RisingWave processes sensitive data in files or tables mirrored into the shared workspace
IF Claude Code reads those files or git history and includes them in its responses
mitigations: Use separate workspaces and repositories
Restrict Claude Code to a scrubbed subset of files
Rotate or redact secrets before either agent touches the workspace
Audit outputs for sensitive strings before sharing externally
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on the workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code has unrestricted filesystem write, modify_git_state, shell, subprocess, and broad network egress; RisingWave is a mutable data-engineering system. The pair therefore overlaps on shared mutable resources, and Claude Code explicitly shares state via filesystem and git only. With no locking or coordination documented for RisingWave, concurrent writes can corrupt repo or workspace state by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or working directory
IF RisingWave or its outputs modify files that Claude Code also edits
mitigations: Run the agents on separate clones
Serialize writes with a lock file
Assign one agent read-only access to the shared repo
Commit frequently to reduce conflict windows
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can act on files and git state, so if it consumes RisingWave-produced artifacts as authoritative, downstream mistakes can propagate into edits or commits. RisingWave is a data-engineering system, but the pair lacks documented verification or provenance checks. This is an inferred interaction, so uncertainty pushes the severity upward from low to medium.
conditions: IF Claude Code uses RisingWave output as input without a verification step
IF that output contains incorrect schema, facts, or generated code
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before acting on generated artifacts
Require tests or schema checks before commits
Keep RisingWave outputs in a staging directory
Use explicit approval for any git write
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and shell environment data, while RisingWave is an open-source data-engineering system with no stated residency or retention constraints in the profile. The pair does not document a specific compliance mismatch, but if regulated data is routed through the shared workspace, policy gaps could arise. Only Claude Code is cited because the profile contains the relevant compliance-sensitive fields; RisingWave lacks such fields.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF Claude Code logs or transmits secrets or regulated content outside approved boundaries
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Mask secrets before invoking Claude Code
Review retention settings for any logs or transcripts
Document data-handling boundaries for the pair
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
